title: The gentle form returns
hookLine: after the thousand suns, the friend's face comes back, and Arjuna can breathe again

lines: A SMALL LAMP, A FAMILIAR FACE.
SHOW ME THE FORM I KNOW.
cards: A child wakes from a nightmare, shaking in the dark. A parent comes in and turns on the small lamp by the bed. Same room.
Same shadows in the corners. But now there's a familiar face, and a voice that says, it's okay, I'm here. The child can breathe again.
Arjuna has seen the whole universe blazing in Krishna's body, mouths and fire and time itself. And he asked: please, show me the form I know.

teach.h: NO ONE BUT YOU HAS SEEN IT.
teach.b: Verse forty-seven: out of grace, through my own power, I showed you this highest form, full of light, universal, infinite, first. No one but you has seen it before.

Verse forty-eight: not by the Vedas, not by sacrifice, not by study, not by gifts, not by rituals, not by fierce austerities can I be seen in this form by anyone but you. Then verse forty-nine, the tender turn.
Don't be afraid. Don't be bewildered by this terrible form of mine. Let your fear go, be glad at heart, and see my familiar form again.
Sanjaya tells what happens. Krishna shows his own form again, and, becoming gentle in form, saumya, the great soul comforts the frightened Arjuna.
Saumya is a lovely word: gentle, mild, moon-like, cool after heat. Arjuna, verse fifty-one: seeing this gentle human form of yours, I'm myself again. I've come back to my nature.
Then Krishna says what the whole chapter was pointing at. This form is very hard to see; even the gods long to see it. Not by Vedas, not by austerity, not by gifts or sacrifice.
By devotion alone, bhakti, undivided, can I be known like this, seen truly, and entered.

And the chapter's last verse, which some call the essence of the whole Gita: whoever works for me, holds me as the goal, is devoted to me, free of attachment, and without hatred toward any being, comes to me.
After the thousand suns, the friend's face, and the way to it: by devotion alone.

how: Much Hindu worship is directed to God in a gentle, familiar form, an image of Krishna, Rama, Shiva or the Goddess, and many devotees cite Gita 11.54–55 to say that loving devotion, not ritual alone, is how God is truly known.

o: gentle and mild, cool like moonlight
fierce and blazing, like the sun
small and humble, like a servant

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.

s: Krishna says study and sacrifice are enough to see this form
verses 48 and 53: not by Vedas, sacrifice, study, gifts or austerity, but by devotion alone.
Arjuna says he feels himself again when he sees the gentle form
verse 51: seeing your gentle human form, I'm myself again.
the last verse of chapter 11 includes freedom from hatred toward any being
verse 55: without enmity toward any being, the devotee comes to him.

games.q: Krishna says his cosmic form can't be seen by Vedas, sacrifice, study or austerity. then how can it be known?
games.why: by devotion alone, verse 54: bhaktya tv ananyaya, by undivided devotion he can be known, seen, and entered.

practice: Breathe out slowly, as if after a fright, and let your shoulders drop. Picture a familiar, gentle face, of God if you pray, or of someone who has comforted you, and let it say what Krishna said: don't be afraid.
Stay with the gentleness, cool and quiet, like moonlight.

wordCard.voice: Saumya. Gentle, mild, moon-like: the form Krishna takes again after the vision, comforting the frightened Arjuna. He says he's truly seen by devotion alone.

orig.note: Sanskrit: saumya, gentle, mild, moon-like; the gentle form Krishna takes again in 11.50.

carryVoice: Your line: by devotion alone. Saumya, gentle as moonlight after the heat. Two hundred days, and counting.
